params.why: if y = -x then the point lies on the line of symmetry and is its own reflection, so there is nothing to find

stem: Given the function: $xy={=k}$ . The line $y=-x$ is a line of symmetry of its graph. A point on the graph has $x$-value ${=p}$ . Find the coordinates of the point on the graph that is symmetrical to it about the line $y=-x$. Give your answer as $(x, y)$.
solution: Find the $y$-value of the point by substituting $x={=p}$ into the function: $y=\frac{{=k}}{{=p}}={=q}$ .
So the point on the graph is $({=p}, {=q})$ . Check: $({=p})({=q})={=k}$ , so it satisfies $xy={=k}$ .
Reflecting a point in the line $y=-x$ swaps its two coordinates and changes the sign of each: $(x, y)\rightarrow(-y, -x)$ .
Check that the new point is also on the graph: $({=rx})({=ry})={=k}$ , so the point symmetrical to it about $y=-x$ is $({=rx}, {=ry})$ .
notes: Advanced = two of the book's own steps chained: ex6-4-6c (substitute an x-value into xy = k to get y) and then ex6-4-6f (find the point symmetrical about y = -x). k is always negative, as in the book's xy = -6, so y = -x is the line the book pairs with this graph. The x-value is a signed divisor of |k| so y is always a whole number; the point is never on y = -x itself (require). Reflection rule in y = -x is (x, y) -> (-y, -x); the book's own example (-2, 3) -> (-3, 2) agrees. The common slip is to swap without changing signs (reflecting in y = x), which also lands on the graph, so the final check does not catch it; the stem names the line explicitly. All values are whole numbers, so the plain marker answer has no fractions or decimals. Item ids read q:g10m6s4-1-1:g001-symmet.
